Declarative feature nodes

Source: R/feature-pipeline.R
feature_node.Rd

A feature node is a single, self-contained step of a feature_pipeline(). It declares

  • inputs: the columns it is allowed to read,

  • outputs: the columns it produces,

  • depends: the nodes that must run before it.

The node function fn receives a tsibble that holds the key and index columns plus only the declared inputs, grouped by the key so that time-series operations such as dplyr::lag() stay within each series. It must return a data frame holding the key, the index and its outputs. The returned rows may be in any order: they are matched back on key and index.

Usage

feature_node(
  name,
  fn,
  outputs,
  inputs = character(),
  depends = character(),
  stage = c("both", "history", "future")
)

Arguments

name

A single string identifying the node. Other nodes refer to it in their depends.

fn

A function (or purrr-style lambda) that computes the node. It takes a single tsibble and returns a data frame.

outputs

A character vector of the column names fn produces.

inputs

A character vector of the column names fn is allowed to read.

depends

A character vector of node names that must be computed first. Dependencies implied by an input matching another node's outputs are added automatically.

stage

One of "both" (default), "history" or "future", indicating the table(s) the node applies to. Only "both" and "history" nodes run on the historical table; only "both" and "future" nodes run on the future table.

Value

A feature node specification.

See also

feature_pipeline(), compute_features(), feature_forecast()

Examples

# A lagged input, computed per series
lag_x <- feature_node(
  "lag_x", function(x) dplyr::mutate(x, x_lag = dplyr::lag(x)),
  outputs = "x_lag", inputs = "x"
)
lag_x
#> <feature node> lag_x (both)
#>  inputs:  `x`
#>  outputs: `x_lag`
#>  depends: (none)
